newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Jet fuel firm on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Jet fuel firm on tight supplies.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel swaps firmed in late afternoon trading on Wednesday on talks of tightening regional supplies and renewed buying interest from North Asia, traders said.

The December jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) bid rose to $1.25 a barrel from the morning's $1.05/$1.20 quote, brokers said. January regrade also rose to $1.40/$1.70 from an earlier $1.20/$1.75, they said.
"Refiners are optimising gas oil which has reduced jet fuel availabilities," one trader said.

Japan earlier this week bought a 30,000-tonne cargo for arrival in mid-December at $1.75 per barrel premium to Singpaore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, up 10 cents from its last deal, traders said.
December gas oil swaps were largely unchanged from this morning in quiet trade. It was last quoted at $30.50/$30.60 a barrel, up from Tuesday's $30.20/30.30, brokers said.
December gas oil traded in the afternoon at $30.55.
Trader said that the market is firm on renewed buying interest from China and higher prices in the west which has closed the arbitrage window.
December gas oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) opened up $2.25 to $224.50 per tonne.
Fuel oil remained unchanged from from Tuesday with December quoted at $118.00/$119.00 per tonne and January at $117.00/$118.00.
Naphtha was quoted higher on firmer crude values in very thin trade, with December swaps quoted at $22.90/$23.10, up from Tuesday's $22.65/$22.75, one broker said.
